name: Worship and the Regulative Principle
path: Ecclesiology: The Doctrine of the Church

objectives.text: Identify the one true God as the only one people are to worship
Name the things God's people do when the church gathers to worship, such as praying, singing, hearing the Bible read and preached, and giving
Recite the second commandment and explain in simple words that God tells us how He is to be worshiped
Retell the account of the golden calf and explain why God was displeased even though the people called it a feast to the LORD
Describe ways Scripture shows God's people expressing reverence in worship, such as bowing, kneeling, standing for the reading of the Word, and singing together
Explain what Jesus meant when He said God seeks worshipers who worship in spirit and in truth
Explain from Isaiah and Jesus' teaching why God rejects worship offered with the lips while the heart is far from Him
Retell the account of Nadab and Abihu and explain what it teaches about offering God worship He has not commanded

Match each part of a Lord's Day service, such as the call to worship, confession of sin, Scripture reading, sermon, prayer, singing, offering, and benediction, to a passage of Scripture that supports it
Explain why Christians gather for public worship on the first day of the week, using New Testament evidence
Explain the Reformed teaching that worship is to be given to the triune God alone through the one Mediator Jesus Christ and not to angels, saints, or images
Define the regulative principle of worship as the Reformed teaching that God may be worshiped only in the ways He has appointed in Scripture
Explain the difference between offering all of life to God as worship and the gathered public worship of the church
Analyze Old Testament passages in which God rejects worship He did not command and identify the principle they share
Interpret the second commandment as the catechisms do, forbidding both images and any manner of worship not appointed in God's Word
Distinguish the elements of worship from its circumstances, such as time, place, and order of service, and explain how each is to be determined
Identify the ordinary and occasional elements of worship listed in the Westminster Confession and support each with New Testament texts
Explain why Paul describes humanly devised religious rules as self-made religion and how this supports the regulative principle
Compare the regulative principle with the normative principle of worship held in the Lutheran and Anglican traditions
Explain how the regulative principle protects the conscience of worshipers from being bound by the commandments of men
Describe how Reformers such as Calvin and Knox reformed public worship and summarize the biblical reasons they gave for removing medieval practices
Construct a biblical and confessional defense of the regulative principle of worship that answers common objections
Evaluate pragmatic and entertainment-driven worship practices by the standard of what God has commanded in Scripture
Evaluate the arguments made within the Reformed tradition about exclusive psalmody, hymns, and musical instruments in public worship
Design an order of worship for a Lord's Day service and justify each element and circumstance from Scripture and the Reformed confessions

changes: Kept and reworded real competencies (only God is worshiped, naming acts of worship, second commandment, spirit and truth, commanded elements, regulative vs normative comparison, Lord's Day, Colossians 2 self-made religion, defense of the principle, evaluating pragmatism). Recast the heart-worship and reverence items as knowledge and describable practice rather than inner experience. Merged the duplicate elements objectives into a grade 5 service-matching task and a grade 9 confessional task. Dropped the vague grade 11 defense duplicate and the grade 12 synthesis filler. Added the golden calf, Nadab and Abihu, Old Testament rejections of uncommanded worship, worship through the Mediator alone, life worship vs gathered worship, elements vs circumstances, liberty of conscience, Reformation history, the psalmody and instruments debate, and a capstone order of worship. Added verse-level references and confession citations (WCF 1.6, 20.2, 21.1-21.7, WSC Q46-Q59, WLC Q108-Q109, HC Q96 and Q98, Belgic 32) and left sacramental doctrine to its sibling sub-topic.
